This is a tough one. I love SAO and playing this game and even during the play test got me all giddy inside. The VA and everything I think is really well done. There are some gripes with combat, but quickly overlooked when you get more into it. 

If you love SAO, the VA, and the world itself, buy this game. You'll love it. 

On a personal note, I'm a bit angry. The game has no business being this expensive, with day 1 character dlc and a rotating in-game shop for skins. If the game was a quarter of the price then for sure I can see it being a possibility, but given that this is a live service game, you need the playerbase to be alive. Having a high price tag is already dissuading. I can probably get my 50-60 hours out of it in a couple months, but after a few months, I'm fearful for the player population, especially for the large battles. I don't know why Japanese devs do this, they always price their games right at market maxes, despite what type of game it'll be. I think a lot of people would gladly spend a bit on skins and characters if the initial entry fee wasn't so brutal. 

Another glaring issue that shocked me was that there is no guild system - which is something that'd be super important later on. Even voice chat or an easy way to type chat (graned it's cross-play, but for an MMO come on!). 

All that being said, if cost isn't a concern and you just want a decent SAO game, then I'd say this is a great game.

As an SAO fan, I was lucky to get to try the game early in the Closed Beta Test, and from that I immediately knew that I wanted this game badly. Fast forward to now, I would say that this game did not disappoint me, despite its quirks. The character rigging is weird during cutscenes, blocking and dodging can be hard due to the delay and stuff, the map doesn't show the edge of the map makes exploration a tad bit more annoying, the way you start at level 1 on every coop game can get tiring, etc. It's definitely nowhere near perfect, but in a way, that's the charm of SAO games. It basically hits all the marks I expect from an SAO game.

With that being said, this game is definitely not for everyone. If you're one of the people who tells people to buy Grandblue Fantasy Relink instead, you're kinda missing the point of this game. We play and like it because it's SAO, and to me, this is one of the better games in this IP. It kinda has the vibes of Fatal Bullet, but with SAO elements and uncapped fps. If you're not into SAO or you only just knew about SAO, I wouldn't really recommend this game especially at these prices, and you're probably be better off buying that other game or play earlier SAO games to familiarize yourself with SAO games as I personally think this isn't the best game to start the journey. I might be biased, but that's kinda the whole point with games based off of IPs.

Game is good, story is interesting so far (few missions in), feels like a semi-fresh start for the game series. Runs well, polished (no bugs or connection issues out of the gate), and combat is that of a third-person character action game, with soft-roles you would see in any other MMO-like game. Menus are a tad on the heavy side, and Campaign has two difficulties.

For people interested; look up Havian on YouTube and look at his impressions video. If you bought into the game for the Advanced Access, either you were impressed by the Open Beta to buy in or you were already a fan.

For cosmetics, the co-op quests and boss raids have a chance to drop one of several cosmetics (as in, theres a handful per specific quest/raid) upon completion. There are also cosmetics in campaign missions (they look like the exact same ones in the cash shop so maybe reskins?) that give a bit more replay-ability. You can permanently upgrade characters the more you use them or by spending in-game earned currency on memories. There IS a lot here on display and with a roadmap planned for the next bit, for people invested it will be worth it. My wife says the only gripe in the first few missions is "we don't know whats going on" but believes more story beats will hit when we clear more.

Yes there is a cash slop shop, and it looks like every 30 days, if you run the course of the single-track battle pass, you get enough tickets to get a single set of cosmetics. There is NO gatcha to this. I would even say play the campaign and get all of the cosmetics to show off.
I am a slut for SAO so shelling out enough for me and my wife to get all the cosmetics out of the gate is par for the course, but I ABSOLUTELY understand that those more conscious with their funds will get more value spending elsewhere on a game they enjoy.

TL;DR
If you are a SAO fan, it will be fun.

I know I don't have much playtime, as I literally just played through the tutorial, but I have posted a review on pretty much every SAO game on steam outside of IF so here are my first look thoughts:

1 - Combat feels good to use. It is a bit different from all of the other games, being most similar to that of IF. I may just not have played far enough, but it looks like the art chaining isn't in this one
2 - The game has a season pass. I haven't played enough to get an idea on how balanced it is.
3 - The game has LITERALLY Pre-launch Microtransactions... Sure, its all cosmetics, but even still... It looks like the currency you can get in game, but I haven't played far enough to know for sure.

This being said, these are all first looks in. Like I said, I just barely made it through the tutorial. 
- Gameplay feels great. 
- The Menu feels like it is based heavily off Free To Play FPS style games such as Halo Infinite and Splitgate.
- Several of the previous games Recollections and Memories are viewable in game. This includes Infinite Moment (Which isn't on steam), but does not include Last Recollection.
- Bonus items if you have Fatal Bullet. Maybe later other games will support this too.

Premium Edition:
I would not recommend getting this right now unless you REALLY want the artbook or Soundtrack. This being said, it does come with something not listed in the comparison chart - A survivors type minigame with Kirito. This can easily be beaten, and you can get every item and max them out in a single run. This costs an additional $40 at the time of writing, and while the soundtrack is great, and the art is cool, it is not worth the extra $40

Tl;Dr - If you like SAO, this game is a good one to play with friends. I would recommend waiting for a sale though, as I feel like it doesn't quite warrant $60.

The multiplayer aspect enhances the fun, allowing for seamless co-op battles and an opportunity to bond with other players in a shared journey through this fractured dreamscape.

In short, Sword Art Online: Fractured Daydream is a must-play for both long-time fans of the series and newcomers alike. Must-play for SAO enjoyers. It's gorgeous, fun, authentic and the music feels straight out of a 2000s eastern MMO game (good). The character interactions are endearing and often funny, cute, wise or emotional. The way characters smile after delivering a line of dialogue is adorable, and the lipsync tech they used is very enjoyable to look at.

The combat is satisfying for several reasons, but I think the one I'd like to bring up is the iconic red slices that appear as your blade slashes an enemy, accurately displaying where your attack landed. Combine that with weak points on monsters and it makes for a combat system that feels very deliberate and cool.

Every character feels unique to play as because of their different abilities. Not just attacks, but movement as well. There is some skill overlap of course, so as you play the game and increase your familiarity with the mechanics, you'll get better with every character. So don't hesitate to try them all. Loot is fun to collect and I love that there's alternate outfits and accessories to find in each level.

Overall the game has a very pleasant atmosphere that sucks you in and makes you want to keep existing in its world. A rare sight indeed these days. Of course, you should watch at least a couple seasons of SAO before playing this, as it is a game for the fans.

Speaking of, this game is so good it got me to watch Ordinal Scale and start Alicization as well. I basically wake up every day and put on my metaphorical NerveGear to watch SAO, before fulldiving into this game and experiencing more SAO. Then I go to bed and dream about SAO. This game really makes you FEEL like Kazuto Kirigaya.

I don't usually write reviews, but I feel like I have to say how amazing and underrated this game truly is. I tried playing previous SAO titles as they were coming out through the years, mind you they were on consoles and might I add not the greatest game series I have played. Which is why I have decided to write a review on this game.

[b] Story [/b] The story in this SAO title is a lot better than the last games. This time around the story takes place after the main anime, so they had a ton of freedom to really do something they wanted here, which really shows. The story is unique enough to have kept me quite engaged. As you progress through the story, you slowly unlock characters to use in the amazing multiplayer 20 man raid, which might I add is insanely addicting and very fun to play.

[b] Multiplayer [/b] This in my opinion is the main reason I am writing this review. I haven't played a game with such addicting multiplayer game-play in years. There are three different multiplayer options you can choose from after completing the main story, being free roam, co-op quests and boss raids. These three online modes are all extremely populated, which are always absolutely popping off no matter the time of day at the time of writing this review, mainly because this SAO game has cross-platform play, ignore steam charts as this game easily has 50,000 people playing at any given time. The combat feels insanely fluid, the mobs feel fleshed out, the zones are beautiful and the community in this game are very helpful. Even if on the very slight chance you find a quite game, you will wait max 60 seconds before you are placed into a co-op mode that fills the remaining player spots with bots until another minute later the lobby rapidly fills with players. 

I would rate this game a solid [b] 9.0/10 [/b]

[h1] The Best SAO Game [/h1]

[b] What I Liked [/b]

I'll start this off by saying the point of the game isn't the story.  The story isn't bad.  There are only so many ways stories in SAO can play out.  The story is the only way they could justify bringing in characters from the anime over.  That being said, if you're a fan of SAO, then you'll like the story.

The combat is where the game shines.  I've tried a few SAO games over the years, and none of them felt quite right.  This one though makes me feel like I'm in SAO.  The characters move and play like they would in SAO.  The enemies behave as if they are their counterparts in the anime.  The combat is great.

Of course, the point of the game is the grind.  It's a huge, huge grind.  It's all about leveling up and grinding for gear.  Doesn't make it bad at all.  With 21 characters, there is a ton to grind for.

The graphics are good, and again, I feel like I am in SAO.  I wish more locations from the anime were in the game, but it's good for what it does.

[b] What I Did Not Like [/b]

I'm an old guy, so the game hurts my hands after awhile.  There is a bunch of button mashing.  More than likely I'll have to give it up because it's too hard on my hands.

Playing online is the primary point of the game.  Doing co-op dungeons and boss fights.  The problem is that will get boring after awhile since there isn't a huge variety of areas.  The other issue is that the player population is low, and half the time bots filled in for a live person.  But, they were decent bots who fulfilled their role decently enough.

Day one DLC is also a downer, along with microtransactions.  They aren't required though.

[b] Why I Stopped Playing [/b]

Haven't yet, expect I will once it bothers my hands too much and I tire of the grind.

Problems, in no short order:
[i]Most, if not all, servers are based within Japan.[/i] Previously, there were three distinct regions: NA, EU, and JP. All the servers were consolidated together due to low player population on any server that wasn't JP during most hours. Unless you're playing single-player, you'll probably have 200+ ping if you're non-JP.
[i]Slow update cycles, for those who are inclined.[/i] The development team [b]seems[/b] to be relatively small. While they're dedicated towards this game, the amount of content they can churn out may be a bit of a turn-off for those who are expecting substantial updates per season.
[i]Always-on(ish) game.[/i] The game can be played in single-player and offline in limited function but key things will be missing. Any DLC characters will be disabled until you reconnect. Any shop-bought cosmetics, for those who prefer fashion before form, will also be disabled.
The core gameplay is tied to the online matches, so you'll be unable to enjoy the full experience offline. [b]They are testing a single-player/offline mode that allows for full access to the game. Props to them.[/b]


Aside from those problems, the core gameplay of a dungeon-raiding/boss fight experience is highly tuned though. 
Balancing in-game ensures no character is particularly weak, nor is a specific character a must-have for a team setup. Most characters have a clear identity within their class, and there's few instances of "oh this character is just x but better".
[u]Ignoring the latency problems[/u], all the bosses have clear reads via the damage indicators that appear.
The various equipment items you can equip have a degree of customizability, and can be tailored for a specific experience or boss. [i]The entire end-game turns into a loadout-setup simulator essentially. If you enjoy it, bonus content for you![/i]

Only about a week in so far, so I'm in the honey moon phase, so keep that in mind. Also keep in mind the main selling point of the game is the multiplayer.

In terms of SAO games this one is a breath of fresh air.  DIMPS is now 2 for 2 on their track record for making games I enjoy in this IP.  Combat definitely takes some getting used to, you can dash cancel out of your normal attacks but can't cancel out of skills or ultimate.  Ultimate isn't a problem because you have Invulnerability during the animation.  For skills, you just need to be a bit careful and not lock yourself into one during an attack, or just put some effort into positioning.

Story was IMO pretty mid, it was inoffensive but nothing that hasn't been seen before and didn't take any risks.  I'd compare it to room temperature water.  It's not bad but it's not exciting either.

Progression I am super mixed on.  I like the amount of things there are for me to unlock, and I don't mind that it's pretty grindy and slow progression wise, but for a lote of people I imagine it might be a bit of a deal breaker.
Boss Raids, and Co-Op quests have unlock requirements.  You need to have the required Player Rank, and and clear the required Co-Op quests or Boss raid to move onto the next.  Assuming you play through the whole story first, you should be somewhere in the rank 20 range, so you should be able to do the first 3 co-op quests and the first boss raid.  The problem is that the Rank requirements DRASTICALLY increase later on.  If you get bored of running the same few quests over and over, you're not gonna last long enough to unlock the 3rd boss raid.  Which is a big downside because the first 2 boss raids are static, but the 3rd rotates through what the boss will be (I somehow can't remember if it changes daily or weekly).

Now if that sounded bad to you, I have more bad news, which for me is good news because I like grinding but I understand not all do.  Each character has two Passive slots.  Each character has their own passive by default.  Raising a character to Character Rank 30, unlocks that passive to be used on all characters.  This is a problem.  Not all passives are created equal, some are basically dogwater, and some are absurd once you find out the numbers.  You'll probably want passives that benefit whoever you want to main, and for some characters, that means both of those are from other characters.  That means you'll have to level two characters you might hate playing, to build your character the way you want to.  This is a baffling decision because this means you'll have to put in the time to level two characters other than the one you're intending to main.  You also get passive BASE STAT increases at certain character ranks, so two of the same character with exactly the same gear won't perform equally, and because of how multiplicative scaling works, base stats mean a lot.  The reason all of this is a problem is because you're gimping yourself by doing this.  You get extra EXP at end of mission for doing things like getting MVP, which will be harder for you to do against players who only focuses on their mains, because they will simply be doing more damage than you possibly can, and if you're not getting MVP you're getting less EXP and that means having to do more runs of quests, and that means wasting more time.

If you've read this far you're probably willing to read a bit more, and you also might be someone who'd be able to enjoy the game despite these issues, or you're literally just me.  I enjoy super grindy slow burn types of games, so this is actually perfect for me.  I don't know how this game will pan out longterm, but currently I'm having a lot of fun slowly chipping away at stuff, ticking boxes off my checklist of things to grind out.  First 3 dlc characters are funny greatsword girl and two more characters from GGO Alternative, which I really liked so I'm excited for that.  I am able to play as a funny magic lady with big hair who can fly, shoots big lazers, drops a funny sword man on people, and is voiced by Maaya Sakamoto (Jalter and DAO my beloved).  This game doesn't cater to everyone but it certainly caters to ME SPECIFICALLY.  Obviously the game has issues, but what game doesn't in current year.  My last hopes for games to be good were ground into the dirt, poured gasoline on, and burned, by SEGA when they killed PSO2 with the slap in the face that is NGS, which I still play on occasion because I have attachment issues and get overly invested in my MMO characters.  If you play on JP I might see you, if you play NA, still might see you but not as likely.

TL:DR Game grindy, Story Mid, Multiplayer focused, Not perfect but I like it.

It's about what you expect, nothing more, nothing less.

For those that have played Re: Hallowed Fragment, It's very much like that game. The pros are that the graphics, combat and the online coop missions are better. The neutrals are that while the combat is better, it still is stiff and janky, which some might not find acceptable in 2024, there are many frustrating animations and attacks. The negatives are that there are no skill trees and no skill sets. You can not learn new moves and set them, you get 3 skills, a special and an ultimate per character. That is it. It's very bare bones.

For those who have not played Re: Hallowed Fragment, this is a typical looter shooter type game with a lot of problems. For loot, you have 1 weapon and 3 accessories to choose from. You just farm those 4 slots and that's about it. You can rip off effects from legendary/epic items and put them on other legendary/epic items, but that's it. You also have one passive that you start with on each class, and leveling that class to 30 unlocks that passive to be used on all other classes. You can have 2 passives active at once. That's the end of the RPG mechanics.... Bare bones is about the best way to sum up this game.

Story: The story in this game is overall mediocre. I think the PREMISE of the story is great, but it lacks in dialogue and execution. It felt a little rushed, a little lacking and overall underwhelming. I watched all the cutscenes, but found myself WANTING to skip so many of them and I enjoy SAO as a franchise very much, despite the anime also having major problems as well. The Length of the story is about 10-20 hours depending on how much you care about cosmetics, 100% collection and max score, which is... fine, but way, way shorter of a story compared to the other SAO games. This is fine because this game is billed as a live service with a story, not a singleplayer game with multiplayer tacked on, but worth mentioning so people know.

Combat: Very hit and miss. Literally. I love a lot of it, it's the same principle and feel as the other SAO games, with some smoothness added in, but also a ton of jank still left in and even more problems due to monsters having faster attacks and this being more action based than the older games. One step forward, two steps back, basically. Most moves have NO tracking, meaning if you fire them off, especially charged attacks, bosses won't be there when you land it and it will be wasted, this includes your long cooldown ultimates. You get stuck in animations, some of which you are NOT invincible for, and you will get pelted by bosses. They need to fix combat very badly, as fun as it is at times, it's equally frustrating just as often. The dodging is also really bad. You can only dodge in 8 hard directions, not exactly free aim, which makes it feel a bit awkward in this day and age. When locked onto a target, sometimes you will not dodge the way you want to and it causes you to get hit, or you will slam into small enemies and get stuck on them, very, very shitty. Aiming projectile moves is also shitty for similar reasons, I will be locked onto an enemy and aiming right at them, and Healthcliff's projectile shield will shoot to the right and hit nothing.

Maps: The maps are okay. They feel like something out of a 2010-ish game, not a 2024 game, but in terms of variety and overall design, they are fine. There are a lot of instances I will get almost-stuck and have to wiggle out of it. I will hit rocks and have to run around them. Dodging, and this goes into combat as well, is very shitty. You will dodge into a random rock and get hit because of it.

Overall, I am recommending it because I enjoy playing it, despite how shitty it is in a lot of ways. I knew what I was getting when I bought it, and I got a key for $50 off a reputable site. I would not recommending paying more than that, and if you aren't a major SAO fan and haven't played and enjoyed the older games, I wouldn't recommend buying it at all unless it's on sale later for $10 or something. I am hoping they fix it, but knowing Bandai and how their games are, this is probably what we are stuck with, and all we will get are new characters and maps going forward, which may be fine for me, but probably not most people reading this.

Hardcore SAO fans that played/liked the other games:    8/10
Non-SAO fans or people who haven't played the others: 5/10

I like it. I had fun and I'm still having fun at 101 hours in. Some of the people criticizing this game are trying to shame fans for being "numb" to the flaws of the game. They say that they're only saying it's good because it's a "good SAO game". But my experience says otherwise. I'm having a blast.

The Pros:

-The animations are nice.
-Having 20 players to play with every raid or dungeon crawl feels good.
-The loot system is triggering my addiction.
-The stats restrictions on characters and weapons on lower dungeons makes it so that newbies don't feel left out. You're not going to see someone do 20k per hit, while you deal 20 per hit.
-The raid bosses feel great to fight.
-Didn't try to break my graphics card or overheat my PC on launch unlike another certain game that haters keep comparing this to.
-LLENN, Shinohara Miyu (I'm using her real name because STEAM thinks her game name should be censored for some reason), Sinon. Playing as a ranged character just feels amazing.

The cons:

-The camera man has ADHD and will randomly spin 180 sometimes.
-Playing as melee needs getting used to.
-The costumes aka Appearance Items' drop rates are abysmal. I'm not sure what's the rate, but I've been farming the final coop dungeon for 2 days now but I still haven't gotten the item.
-The price feel a bit steep.
-Story mode isn't something to be excited for.
-Some characters can only be unlocked in doing certain chapters of the story mode. Because story mode isn't too good, it becomes a bit of a drag.
-Items called 'mods' are sometimes hard to find, and getting the one you want is even harder. I wish I would get a "crit rate up" every time but instead I get a "guard damage reduction up" on a character THAT DOESN'T HAVE A GUARD FUNCTION. Your luck will really be a big factor in your coop experience.
-Some dungeons encourage speed running the entire thing because if you get left behind, other groups will take all the experience for themselves which means now you're fighting a boss at level 10.

As you see there are more cons than pros so maybe you'd think I won't recommend this game. But... no. It's fun. What can I do? I know many of you hate the anime. There are probably some of you reading this who decided to just hate on the game because it had "SAO" on the title. But the truth is that it's just fun. The feeling of spamming emotes after finishing a dungeon beside others who revived you because you carelessly stood in front of a 1-hit kill mechanic is wholesome. It feels like you're a part of a community who's just enjoying the game for what it is without trying to min max anything. If you're the kind of person who likes competition there's also a ranking page after runs. Being in a 20 player raid gives a different feeling that other games that only allow up to 4 players just can't give. If that's a feeling you're looking for and want to share in, then this game is for you. If it isn't, then go buy Sparking Zero. Either way you'd be giving money to the same company lol.

Adding my old review back when i only had 40 hours on it:

After 40+ hours of this game after buying it on sale I can finally say that all of these people saying the game is dead are liars, this game has never been more alive, and if you don't find people to play with that's most likely because the US and UK servers are empty because everyone is mostly on the Asia server. Does it affect ping if you don't live near Asia (for example you live in South Africa like myself)? No, in fact if you have a stable connection you won't be having any problems with your ping, plus you can freely transfer from servers.

Now for the story and gameplay.
Story: The story of this game is great and it's pretty consistent, the story of the game follows where the anime ended in War of the Underworld, so instead of following the SAO games it follows the anime, so Hollow Fragment, Realization, Lost Song, Alicization Lycoris etc didn't happen in this game's story, so SAO games original characters like Philia, Premiere Kureha and etc aren't in the game.... yet, I say yet because Strea is a game original character from Hollow Fragment and she is a character in the game, as far as I know she has her own unique story in this game that comes with her DLC, the quest reintroduces her into the story in a unique way, we can expect this for other game original characters. I love the interactions between different characters in this game, especially how everyone treats Oberon, even Heathcliff doesn't like him, Eugeo's reaction to Yui was fantastic as well.
Overall story is 8/10.

Gameplay: the combat in this game is extremely good as you can play a total of 21 base game characters from SAO, all with unique skills and passives for each character. All characters have 3 advanced skills, 1 ultimate and 1 unique skill(That's what they call it in game) so a total of 5 different abilities, while for melee characters there is a light and heavy attack in game each also have a charged attack if you hold it and you can do combos from light to heavy, for example : Light, heavy......Light, light, heavy, hold light. The characters won't do the same attacks if you combo chain with heavy, light and charged attacks. there is also a guard and lock on system. For Ranged characters they play the same as they do in Fatal Bullet, they don't have a guard but they can aim and deal a ton of damage if you hit a weak spot, Sinon and Sterben especially are toptier in this game for that reason. There is also a flight system for ALO based characters and Administrator which is MUCHHH better than the flight system in Lost Song and Accel x SAO.
Combat is overall 8/10 as well as I enjoy playing different characters and playing different roles each match.

You remove those substats and put those in your loudout. Only Legendary and Epic stuff can get their substats removed/replaced. Nothing below Epic.

> The problem is, the RNG and lack of rewards is god awful terrible. Rewards are gained from killing the final boss, but what you get may not even be related to the class you're playing, much less the character. And 95% of the boss rewards are blue and below.

> This limits your investment to basically one character if you want the best performance out of said character. 

- Coop Raids/Boss Raids are poorly designed, repetitive, and boring. Naturally, towards higher tier raids, most players are simply rushing towards bosses, as it's our only real incentive for getting any rewards. Nothing in the coop raid offers drops or anything. Just the boss. Time vs Reward. There are clashes within the community against speedrunners, but Dimps is the culprit for enabling this.

- Cheaters do exist, not that I blame them. The lack of rewards and incentives is just that bad. The grind is that bad. Dimps has taken action and threw waves of temporary bans on said cheaters.

I'm loving the game so far, I think that in the future it could get boring if they don't add new bosses, maps and other things to do, there are people saying they are waiting 30 minutes in queue, what a lie! The game adds AI when it no longer finds players and this takes a maximum of 2 to 3 minutes... There are still a lot of people playing, just choose the correct region according to timezone that there are people playing like switching to Asia sometimes (the ping is ok and at least I don't have lag)..

I loved the game in so many ways, mainly for mixing common mechanics with those of ALO and GGO. I believe that the game still needs some "repeated" characters but in other classes, for example Asuna from GGO and ALO.

The main story didn't hold me as much... I just played to unlock the characters, but the online makes up for it, I know a lot of people expected it to be a large-scale SAO MMORPG but this game is enough to have fun.

The game is very niche so it may not appeal to such a large audience, but it's a good game anyway.

I believe the graphics are ok, but the combat needs to improve (for example: you can get stuck with enemies when you try to dodge, there are long-range enemies and sometimes you have your sights fixed on another and can't see the attacks behind you) so it can be very easy to die because of it. I loved the skills and combat mechanics other than that, the number of bosses is not that large but for now it is enough.

I also believe that the free-roam mode could have more enemies, have a bigger map, have dungeons and quests to do in groups or solo. and the timer for the instance to end is a little bad, it should be unlimited and players can join the sessions that are already in progress if they are not full.

In general I loved the game, it's a really fun game, it's something I've always wanted (to play with more people on a large scale) the only negative point is that I've always been waiting for one mmorpg and not just 20 (which I don't always find because sometimes we fall for AI) I bought it at full price and in my country it is very expensive, but I recommend it on sale.

The game runs surprisingly well on Linux, with only minor technical hiccups. The most notable issue was the mouse sensitivity being too low even at maximum settings, though I managed to solve this with a custom script. The keyboard and mouse controls could use some polish - while generally functional, menu navigation can be awkward, particularly when crafting spheres where you can select items with the mouse but not affixes.

The visual presentation truly shines with proper anime-style character models that stay faithful to the source material (no weak western monstrosities like we often see in recent AAA releases). While the characters are undeniably charming, I slightly miss that classic season 1 fanservice magic. The character roster is impressively varied, offering plenty of choices with distinct playstyles and abilities. The cutscenes are particularly well-crafted, bringing the story to life in true SAO fashion.

Regarding monetization, it's a mixed bag. While the base game is a one-time purchase, there's a cosmetic cash shop and character DLCs. The monthly quest system (battle pass) offers some premium currency, but the rewards have become less generous - previously enough for one dress pack out of three, now not even that much.

The multiplayer aspects are quite engaging - from cooperative scenarios to boss raids and free roam. However, the long-term enjoyment might depend on your grinding tolerance and the pace of new content releases.

For SAO fans, this is definitely a must-buy that captures the essence of the series. Others might want to watch some multiplayer gameplay videos first, as the story alone might not justify the price tag if you're unfamiliar with the characters and universe.

If you are an SAO fan it's worth every penny. This game is a love letter to the fans, its packed with fan service moments (not the ecchi kind); the writing and interaction between characters is perfect, every line is voice acted (Japanese Dub). The main story is basically another season of SAO that takes place right after the War of the Underworld Arc; it does not continue the gameverse canon so most game original characters will probably not be playable/appear. Cutscenes are all 3D in-game engine, similar to Alicization Lycoris but better, with some pre-rendered 3D animation cutscenes for the fights. Without skipping cutscenes, it took me about 25 hours to finish the main story. 

If you are an SAO fan and you love the characters & universe and want to see your favorite characters interact with characters from different seasons in ways you never would of thought (kind-of like Isekai Quartet), you'll enjoy the story.

The multiplayer is essentially Fatal Bullet with more melee weapons & special attacks added, but without the main city hub, unique player character, or PvP. You need to progress through the main story to unlock characters for use in multiplayer, so keep that in mind if you are thinking of buying it just for the multiplayer. It isn't a traditional RPG like Hollow Realization/Alicization Lycoris so if you do not like the gameplay loop of grinding the same 3-5 dungeons (with slightly different variations of tasks & enemies) to unlock new skins or experimenting with different characters and classes this game may not be for you. If you liked the PvE in Fatal Bullet you will probably like this game.

The combat is greatest it has ever been for an SAO game: You have a Basic Attack & Alternate Basic Attack, Heavy Attack & Alternate Heavy Attack, 3 Skills and an Ultimate, all of which are unique to each character, as well as Dodge and Block. Each character's playstyle is completely different, if you are great with 1 character if will not translate to another. It's a lot like a fighting game in that aspect. The only complaint I have would be that the skills do not follow enemies, if you activate a skill and the enemy moves, your character will not follow and you are just stuck attacking air; everything else feels fluid though.

The leveling can get grindy & repetitive, but each character has a completely different moveset which helps keep things fresh; no two characters are alike. There is an overall player rank and each character has their own rank; as you level up player rank you unlock harder difficulties and leveling up characters unlocks new skins and emotes. There are weapon skins, overall appearance skins, and 2 accessory slots you can customize per character.

In Co-Op you complete various tasks in Aincrad, GGO, OS, or Underworld maps with 5 squads of 4 eventually fighting a boss depending on the map. There is no voice chat, only a preset emote wheel. If there are not enough players, AI fills them in taking into account the real player's classes to ensure parties are well rounded (has a healer, tank, etc.). As players join they replace the AI. The AI is skilled enough that you wouldn't notice the difference between a team of AI vs Real Players, except maybe that your AI teammates revive you more reliably & stick with you. You can pre-select your favorite character so you don't get matched with another player who uses that character, but there may be duplicates in another squad. There's about 3 stages in each mission that you teleport between: the first stage you are just in your squad of 4, the second stage you meet up with other squads, and the last stage of the map is the boss. Each game can take about 20-30 minutes. As you go up in difficulty there are new/additional enemies/mechanics added to the maps & bosses; the enemies never felt like they just have more health/tanky. The enemies have just the right amount of health as you would expect them to; they are not sponges like in Alicization Lycoris or Last Recollection.

In Boss Raids you only fight more difficult bosses that do not appear in Co-Op, which can take about 20 minutes. There's also a solo mode where you fight waves of enemies with just 1 character and no healing items. 

Both Co-Op and Boss Raid Modes have unique appearance items that the bosses can drop but they are pretty rare. There are micro-transactions but they are purely cosmetic, some of them can change the character's ultimate slightly. The equipment crafting is a RNG/gacha system but using the in-game currency. There are common, rare, epic, and legendary classes of gear/weapons that you can upgrade; legendary class weapons/gear can change the way your weapon skills work or give you permanent status buffs/debuffs that incentivize you to change your playstyle.

The multiplayer makes you feel like you are clearing floors in Aincrad with other real players. I can definitely see myself sinking well over 100+ hours into this game. Recommended if you like the Dungeon-Raid gameplay loop.

[b][u]tldr: It's an okay game at best, a terrible deal at full price.[/u][/b]

[h2][b] General Controls [/b][/h2]
I will preface that I only played on M&KB. General movement feels pretty clunky, you are animation-locked when doing attacks and can only dodge out of it once every couple of seconds or so. This will likely lead to getting hit more often than not if you're button mashing or a considerable DPS loss if you're playing cautiously which feels bad either way.
There's quite a few bits of random geometry you tend to get caught on in the coop maps which is pretty annoying but can be jumped out of which doesn't make it too big of a deal
Flying characters make traversal pretty good but unless you pick em in multiplayer, you're stuck on ground movement which I am not a fan of.

[h2][b] Combat [/b][/h2]
[h3][u]Animation Lock[/u][/h3]
I fucking hate this shit, when you use skills, you are locked into whatever move the skill entails, a considerable number of them will be carried out while stationary and if the target moves, every attack is gonna miss.
Other attacks have some jank-ass movement direction/attack interaction, [i] cough, cough, LLENN S1 [/i] which will lead to you missing all of your attack along the direction of your path and/or cause you to be out of position and eat some fat damage.

[h3][u]Leveling[/u][/h3]
Locking skills behind levels during multiplayer feels pretty bad. Taking away tools from your already limited skillset and putting it behind a mandatory time-gate every multiplayer match feels more akin to a chore than an enjoyable experience

[h3][u]Enemy boss[/u][/h3]
Call this skill issue or whatever, damn near all of the bosses I have seen so far are huge compared to the player with equal large hitboxes.  Granted, sometimes, you can just stand under a boss and chomp at its ankles until it progresses phases and some attacks are telegraphed well with an indication on the ground.

But some attacks feel like they come out without warning, and if you're playing melee while under the boss, the camera is going to bump against the ceiling and limit visibility pretty badly. This exacerbates the feeling of unfairness despite the telegraphed nature of some attacks.
If you're playing ranged, however, some ranged attacks' only indication is the projectiles that are spawned and homing in on you. As a ranged DPS, you have no block, so you better time your dodge otherwise you're eating 1/3 of your hp to a reaction check. Additionally, some ranged attacks have such a wide range that you can't run out of it in time and have to dodge it, without a clear understanding of when your i-frames are during said dodges, you're gonna get hit for like 1/2 your hp.

[h2]Other stuff I can't be bothered to catagorise[/h2]
[h3]Equipment[/h3]
The equipment system sucks, you can't reroll substats and have to rely on RNG rolling 6 times in your favour in order to get a half-way decent weapon.
But you can still do good damage or have good survivabilitywithout perfect rolls, so I guess that's fine? Don't like it tho.

[h3]Battle Pass[/h3]
I honestly don't much care for this system, I get that the dailies/weeklies/whatever wants you to play different classes for forced variety but each multiplayer match is like 10-20mins and unless I can knock out multiple missions in 1 match, it's really not worth the PITA of picking characters/classes I dislike just for 1/5th of the battlepass bar to go up.

[h3]Story Mode[/h3]
The story is meh, the presentation is meh, the locking of characters behind story completion is a source of great annoyance. I want to play all the characters from the start, it's not like the multiplayer is narratively affected by story progression anyway. (I think?)
There's a bunch of unlockable stuff in each story mission but it's a hidden collectible that's a massive PITA to collect all if you want some cosmetics so you gotta look up a guide to catch em all. Without a flying character, traversal is slow if there's a river in the map and you missed a collectible on the other side before crossing.

[h3] For 80 bucks, this was definitely not worth the price tag. I should've gotten ReFantazio instead [/h3]

I wish I had better things to say about Sword Art Online: Fractured Daydream, but unfortunately, this is a major disappointment. Let's start with the combat system—it feels clunky and uninspired. There are so many ways it could be improved, yet it seems like DIMPS didn’t put much thought into making the gameplay feel fluid or rewarding. The frustrating part is that the game doesn’t even use a traditional leveling system for characters. Instead, it forces you into a player ranking system, which just feels disconnected. You’re not building up your character through personal progress—it’s more about grinding and increasing your rank as a player. This system not only limits your sense of progression but also ties into the free roam mode, where your player rank determines the quality of the drops you get. The higher your player rank, the better gear and materials you’ll find in the open world and in crafting, which pushes you further into an endless grind for better loot.

On top of that, you have to constantly grind for better equipment, and the game doesn’t make it fun or rewarding. Equipment is the main way to improve your character, so rather than focusing on leveling up or skill-building, you’re stuck chasing gear to make any meaningful progress. The crafting system is equally shallow, forcing you to gather materials from drops that are gated by your player rank. The whole system lacks balance and depth, making the grind feel more like a chore than actual progression.

One of my biggest gripes is the lack of the ability to create a character. Once again, we’re forced to play as Kirito. Seriously, why? Who actually wants to keep playing as him every single time? The absence of a character creation option is a significant miss, especially in an era where player choice is such a major draw in RPGs. It further adds to the feeling of restriction and repetitiveness.

The story mode isn’t much better. You’re sent off on uninspired objectives—exploring the map, doing time-wasting events, or fighting mini-bosses to unlock some cosmetic rewards. The exploration in the story map feels very restrictive, limiting your ability to wander freely and enjoy the world. Additionally, the game features pickups for health, max HP, and attack power boosts. The more you collect these pickups, the higher the percentage increases for those stats, making them more effective. There’s also an RNG system for perks that come from chests dropped around the map, adding another layer of frustration as you might not get the perks you actually want. However, this system feels tacked on and doesn’t add any real depth to the overall experience. Once you finally reach the main boss, it’s a standard battle, and you get some rewards. It feels more like Memory Defrag in 3D, but with none of the enjoyment. To make things worse, you’re forced to slog through story mode to unlock all the playable characters. This whole system would be more suited for a free-to-play mobile game, not a full-priced console or PC title.

Then there’s the freeroam system, which initially sounds interesting because it supports up to 20 players, but the execution is frustrating. The map is divided into different "regions," each locked behind a level gate, meaning you have to work your way through lower-level areas before gaining access to more difficult regions. This setup slows down exploration, making it feel restrictive instead of exciting. You’re constantly grinding to reach the next region, but the division by levels ruins the flow of the game, especially when you just want to explore freely with other players.

Speaking of the online mode, it’s even more chaotic and poorly designed. Every time you enter an online session, your character is reset to level 1, regardless of how much progress you’ve made in other modes. This destroys any feeling of progression you may have had, forcing you to constantly start from scratch. To make matters worse, nearly everything in the online mode is shared among players—whether it’s resources, enemies, or objectives—except for equipment perks and loot drops. So, while you’re working as a team, you’re still stuck in a race to secure the best gear, creating tension and frustration. Imagine running the same mission repeatedly, finally getting that one piece of gear to drop, only for another player to grab it before you can. Why would they design it like this?

There is, however, a somewhat interesting system where the more you use a specific character, the better they get. You can unlock passives tied to that character, which can then be applied to others. While this idea has potential, it still doesn’t fix the core issues with progression or make the grind feel any more enjoyable.

And don’t get me started on the unnecessary penalty system. You’re penalized if you quit an online session before it ends. Sure, it’s meant to prevent ruining the experience for others, but what if your internet cuts out? Or you have a sudden power outage? Or, worse yet, the game crashes? The penalties get more severe the more this happens, and it feels completely unfair, especially when the circumstances are out of your control.

Oh, and did I mention the battle pass and microtransactions? Yes, this game already has those, adding insult to injury. There are daily and weekly missions tied to the battle pass, pushing players to grind even more for rewards, which only adds to the overall sense of frustration. While the transactions are only for cosmetic items, it still feels like a blatant cash grab after you’ve already spent your hard-earned money on a subpar game. It’s as if they’re saying the initial purchase wasn’t enough.

TL;DR: Sword Art Online: Fractured Daydream suffers from a clunky combat system, a frustrating player rank instead of traditional leveling, a lack of character creation, and a restrictive story mode. The freeroam mode, despite supporting 20 players, feels linear due to level-locked regions. Online play resets characters to level 1 each time, and the grind for equipment and loot drops is tedious. An RNG system for perks adds further frustration, while a cash grab mentality with cosmetic microtransactions and a battle pass leaves players feeling exploited. Overall, the game feels like a disappointing cash-in on the franchise.

I'll keep this review brief, to match the effort by Dimps.

Pros first:
- Visually one of the best looking SAO games.
- Well optimized, runs great on my aging PC.
- The characters look great and are decently animated.
- Same studio that made SAO Fatal Bullet.
- Each character feels unique.
- Some of the story interactions are amusing.

Now cons:
- No custom character, a huge disappointment coming from Dimps.
- The cosmetics drop rate is abysmal, I haven't gotten anything outside of story content.
- The battle pass, while free, is horrid and should not exist.
- Story is entirely skippable, only exists for acquiring minor cosmetics and characters to use in co-op.
- Live service structure with a heavy focus on selling lackluster cosmetic bundles.
- Many skills do not target correctly and will completely miss, especially bad with large AoE skills.
- You can apparently fail to acquire rare loot. I've had items just nope out of my loot list.

I'm trying to enjoy this game, but Dimps has gone out of their way to limit the fun.
I had minimal expectations, but the game decided to disappoint me anyways. If you like SAO, maybe the game's for you. If you wanted to have a decent action RPG, try Granblue Relink instead.

Gearing feels like it needs a refresher, the pool is really big and all over the place. Relies heavy on infusing and getting the right sub-stats placed.

Combat is, sigh. It's not rewarding. With the camera angles being wonky it makes it more difficult to utilize the lock on system. Guarding doesn't always work like you wish it would. The abilities are either OP or not. Very dependent. Enemies can just stand there and knock you while you're using one and not take hit frames. Weakspots are confusing. Elemental damage is a lot to remember as it varies per creature and there is plenty. Attempting to combo mix between Light/Heavy is stressful. 

I don't think I can really do justice reviewing this like others do. But it needs an overhaul. Better advertisement.

This is probably the best sao game we got so far, but it is not without its flaws or issues as a long term sao game player you may already know most of them as the formula is similar.

I'll begin with the good points
-The battle pass is free and gives you tickets to buy outfits in the shop instead of spending more money(I am unsure if ones in the future will be paid, considering sao game track record, I wouldn't put it past them especially considering how dimps handled the fatal bullet dlc)
-The gameplay loop isn't to repetitive or tiring to do, the structure allows it to be entertaining similarly to base pso2 or psu
-Each character plays in a different way be it a minor alteration or larger alteration, if your bored of one you can swap to another and have a mostly different experience
-(potentially good/grey area)The gear is ran off of an affix system, for gear hunters this allows you to hunt for the best gear possible, these affixes will impact your gameplay noticeably or minorly depending on affix build

Neutral: this game is like a roguelite from mission to mission in multiplayer, only your gear carries over

With the good out of the way, there isn't very many actual bad points I can personally make note of so most will seem minor
-The story makes absolutely no sense, if you are familiar with sao you are probably used to this as it is a stable basically(I personally don't mind this considering it is a multiplayer pve game, I would just rather the story make sense or be enjoyable considering it's somewhat forced on you)
-The gear drop rate for legendary items is quite low, for gear hunters like myself finding the best affix combo can be annoying especially with low drop rates and when something does drop it has a potential to have entirely useless affixes(similar to how anthem was at launch, for those not familiar with it an example would be a light element weapon dropping with water damage increase or such)
-This game has a habit of dropping inputs if you use a controller so you may often find yourself just standing there for a moment when you try to combo or use abilities

Overall, despite the issues I would recommend to give it a try depending if you need a game to waste time on, if you have played phantasy star(not new genesis) or previous sao games, you will likely enjoy the gameplay loop provided. There is also a hidden game in the artbook/soundtrack called "Kirito The Hero"

Compared to other polished $60+ action RPG games? It's trash. Compared to a $30 indie game action RPG? It's playable.

Here are some of the things that no one will really talk about because they're fans of SAO and because most of the previous SAO game iterations were even worse, they'll gladly eat this one up despite its rather horrible faults:



-the camera lock on is absolute jank garbage. When you use a skill the camera zooms in on your character, making enemies above, below, and behind you out of your vision. When you do this during a boss fight, the boss will end up out of your camera EVEN WHEN YOU'RE LOCKED ON. And the camera does re-center the boss on your screen, but it feels like it takes forever.

-your characters feel animation locked and movement is generally very clunky. A couple of reasons why this happens is first, your characters do not actually move while attacking much. They feel static and locked in place during animation. Second, the game says you can cancel out of animation to do a dodge/block, but that's not really the case. Third: the game's dash, which also acts as a dodge, makes you dash forward when you do it without pressing any directional keys, instead of backwards. Most action games default dodge without a directional input is backwards, because common sense would let you believe you would dodge things backwards, not forwards. But this game wasn't made with much common sense, apparently.

-maps are rather bland and empty. There are things to collect in the maps during quests, but the game does rather a poor job (or rather, it doesn't do it at all) of actually guiding you towards them in one way or another. You literally have to just mindlessly run around the entire empty, bland map to find these. What they give you also is not well explained. After a quest is done, and you see those collectibles marked as incomplete, all you feel is a sense of conflict as to whether or not it's even worth running around 20 minutes again just to pick up that one data fragment you missed.

-not a lot of enemy and boss variety

-the bosses make no noise. They have no sound. No growl, roar, effect sound before a special move, nothing. Audio is a gigantic part of the immersion, and it's clear the devs have absolutely no understanding of it.

-virtually no sense of progression other than you unlocked the next quest for the story. You don't gain new skills, no passive skill tree of any kind, new gear is just practically the same gear just with higher levels. You can unlock characters to play in multiplayer as you do the quests, but that's only for multiplayer.



If there is one thing the game does well is that you can get a lot of outfits with no MTX just by playing the game, and the multiplayer seems to be decently functional, but that's about it.

The verdict seems to be pretty clear on this one: if you're a fan of SAO, you might enjoy it. If not, wait for a sale. If you really enjoyed Granblue Fantasy Relink like me, and you thought this might scratch your itch, prepare to be disappointed.

As someone who has played all the SAO games this is a great game for a SAO game, but in general it is horrible. You have a cooldown after you dodge once while attacking, the camera is janky, the story is trash but it's fine bc the main thing you will be doing is the co-op quests. These quests are fun for awhile but become extremely monotonous after awhile when you realize you keep getting horrible loot and when you do get good loot it becomes useless because it cost to much resources to constantly level up a good weapon so you have to essential dismantle it if it is epic or higher rarity and get to choose one mod perk on it to transfer to another weapon. Overall everything in this game is so lackluster that it's not even really fun to play anymore. You only have 3 heals per mission which can be annoying at times when you realize besides these three heals few people actually play characters with abilities that heal you and if they do and your not in range you get no healing. 

So essential we have a game with lackluster and clunky combat with a stupid dodge and block system. Missions take around 10-20 minutes and you only get 3 healing items per mission and sometimes there is a statue that refills these heals, but if it is a boss raid there aren't any refills. The loot system is very dull and gives you tons of trash common and common weapons and accessories for the various characters in the game which forces you to go through each and every character and waste time dismantling all of these trash items that keep stacking up. When you eventually get an epic or legendary item it is sometimes decent, but also will have a dumb modifier. For instance, you can get a weapon that deals fire damage that has a modifier on it that says increase water damage by 5%. [b]A neat idea, but complicated execution.[/b]

Fractured Daydream brings 20 players into a raid, to take on parts of a dungeon, only to meet up fighting the end boss together. Only to finish what is a confusing conclusion of this game.

This game wants to be co-operative by working together within your groups and other 16 players, so you don't fail a mission together. Rarely this happens as the game teaches you to grind more, get better gear, and be competitive within the missions. These include getting last hit, highest damage, or better party scores to earn that "MVP" end of the game for more rank/stronger characters faster. So if there's a dead player on the ground that needs reviving, or no tower/STM objective being done before the boss, it's probably because the game wants the players to be competitive. 

I'm not sure to call this a PVE MOBA with competitive scores, or an MMO with lots of repeatable grind, or boss raids if everyone can't work together cause of conflicting objective interests.

When you go through parts of the story, or a couple multiplayer matches... you've done the entire game. The only thing different is having stronger gear (if you're lucky or you grinded it) for the same mission with slightly stronger enemies. There is no other variety in the game, for the price of $80 CAD it should be closer to $30-40. 

The flow of the game is to attack small monsters, gain exp throughout, then fight your way to the boss being 'Awakened level 20-25'. You can unlock skills similar to a MOBA when you level up. No other skills per character are different. Once you beat the boss, you get your fancy drops, some exp for the next dungeon or boss and do it again. 
While the grindy game may be a great way to chill and play with friends, there is not a lot for solo or variety combat to enjoy. 



[h1]The Good stuff;[/h1]
- Returning SAO fans will enjoy the story. Referencing previous games/characters and having good dialouge. 
- Environments look well done, models look good, lots of outfits to try on characters. 
- Daily and Monthly objectives for free battle pass rewards to give players incentive to try new roles.
- Crossplay. Didn't have issues playing with others.



[h1]The lots of bad;[/h1]
- Combat is very stiff, feels like this game is better for 2010 era. Using heavy and light attacks, it's not fluid when your attacks or abilities trying to hit targets. You could be swinging in the air for a while, or missing an entire ability, and not because the enemy moved. Most of the time you will be rushing up to the enemies in hopes to stagger them with your attacks before they can damage you. The auto targetting option does help alleviate some issues, but it makes it harder for flying combat or camera adjustments to prepare oncoming attacks for guard/dodges.

- Dungeons are not engaging, not balanced, and are intentionally frustrating. Since you play the same thing over and over to barely get rank exp, you'll be stuck on the same maps for a while. So you will see them 20-30 levels later again just to do the same tile sets.  
5 different groups are split into 5 starting areas, and they are all not fair or balanced. Some starting areas required more travel, or you have to do an escort, or you will have to travel blue boring teleporters, which result less awakening EXP for that match. So the 4 other groups will have a stronger lead on that. 
There's lots of downtime between rooms so most characters with better speeds have yet another advantage. Ontop of traps, bombs, or annoying "watch outs" that don't add value to the grind or complexity. The hitboxes of the shadow blades are extremely big and sometimes not where you think you see them. All they do is add a layer of frustration to players ontop of the hours of repeated dungeons to grind out gear and dailies for.
The pacing is also bad while you're trying to catch up to the other groups so you don't miss out on other objectives and exp for the missions. Adding onto the slow/stiff combat, it just favouring stronger gear so you spend less time on the first areas.

- Hit boxes from enemy indicators are very inconsistent. Seeing a red circle before a big enemy attack should indicate to the player to be ready, but often these attacks are too early, too late, or worst - show the indicator after the enemy has already attacked. Sometimes you can stand inside those red circle indicators and not take damage. While others when you try to dodge or guard correctly, may not register thus taking damage. 

- Net code for monsters and players. Good luck playing Sniper (Sinon/Sterben) for aiming boss weakpoints where there's a lot of visual effects and CHAIN-EXTENDED-DOWN pop ups in your screen. There's an objective to turn other players attacks off, but it's not enough. You can still see other buffs from support characters on you obscuring view. Ontop of if you rush into rooms too quickly in dungeons, the enemies and attacks will not render properly so there are often times you will get hit by bad hitboxes from attacks, or invisible enemies.

- Game is heavily unoptimized. Recommended is a RTX 2060, while my RTX 3070 on medium settings is at full throttle. The anti-aliasing option seems to be the biggest culprit. But the worst offender is the mouse sensitivity options for PC is TIED TO THE FRAME RATE. Playing at 144 FPS tightens your movement while 30 FPS turns your DPI to 999999. While you go into dungeons and loading areas, your mouse sensitivity continues to change and sometimes fixes itself throughout the run. 
Game also crashes a lot. Changing appearances/outfits before a raid can have a high chance of crashing your game, especially after playing for 3+ hours. Some other folks I played with crash randomly whether it be after 1 hour or 2 hours. 

- Currently there are 12 different queues for modes (except free Roam). So if you don't have 20 players game can fill them with bots. While that may be seem positive, it requires players to know ahead of time otherwise they will rush the boss being underleveled and have a much harder time defeating him.  Without a full group, you spend more time on that map farming enemies during the tower/STM objective. Which is unfair for solo groups cause they get matched with 3 bots. Less EXP for them, which means they will have to play the game more and longer to get rewards. Hopefully this gets fixed in the future or some adjustment with a catchup system.

- Roles are a joke. Having a Tank or a Support just have 1 dedicated skill to 'fit their role' which doesn't seem to fit their playstyles of a team. In reality, tanks and support characters often do as much damage as ranged or fighter role characters, ontop of the benefit/support they give to their team. Heathcliff and Yuna are AOE machines that will pretty much top majority of the time. 

- The UI is definitely made for console. Menus could be a lot better for finding stuff you need. The SAO memories for permanent buffs are placed very deep in the menus and is probably very important to level up to have stronger characters. Whilist items to enchant, move sphere effects, inviting friends, changing equipment or appearances, playing with funny stamps, etc. I'm not sure why most games are going horizontal on menus, when something vertical or lists would be effective and simple. 



[h1]Overall;[/h1]
Game is enjoyable to turn your brain off and grind and that's it. Once you ran a couple of dungeons... you've done pretty much the game. The rest is a cookie clicker and RNG fest for stronger equipment to get higher numbers.

For the price, no. This game needed another year of work. With only a couple of bosses, and reskinned dungeons you need to repeat - it's a conflict between co-operative and competitive gameplay, with no end goal or incentive for players.

**Original Review, additional notes below @ 17 hours**
A shameless cash grab, preying on two groups of people: 1) SAO fans who just wanted a good game to drop to fill their hearts with GGO era vibes(This aint it) and 2) Thirsty whales who want skimpy outfits for children.   Even if you can look beyond that, the game runs terrible even on modern high-end hardware, with stutters and a camera that is tied to the mouse, so if you don't play on controller, get ready to feel like you've got .. a syndrome.  In either event, if this wasn't a gift from a friend I would return it right now.  Instead I'll warn anyone who goes to get it that the devs have taken exactly zero feedback from the open network test, and have in fact made some elements worse.  There are now weird shader elements in cutscenes, the UI in the lobby has even more clunky items to slow you down and keep you looking at their other paid options, because you didn't just pay between $60 and $120? for the game which feels like it's just north of an asset flip but not quite a complete indie game.   There is a battlepass which ironically (so far) seems like the only thing that isn't a cash grab but give it time.  They have DLC bundles for gear and aesthetics, and they have a buggy but built in system for getting RNG boosters to give you more drops, which will undoubtedly be in their bundles.  This is the game that all the youtuber game reviewers warn you not to buy.

**17 hour review notes**
Fractured daydream is an appropriate name for the story since it's what I imagine an AI would think up after reading the wikipedia page for SAO.  There's not really any fundamental lore involved, and 90% of the plot is the characters arguing in an attempt to be cute, 5% of the time is regurgitated plot devices and 5% is actually new/specific to this game lore information.  I could spoil the entire 5 chapters in 2 sentences or less.

The game is abysmal for its inability to properly actuate some skills, like where you hafta mash and hold C/L1 to use your unique skill - i don't know if this is supposed to be a feature so you don't accidentally it, but it's a bad UX.  With the user experience being not worthy of a $19.99 pricetag, the idea that I'm playing on a $100+ version of the game seems about as out of touch with reality as the script writer for this plot.  Graphical bugs, text bugs, and combat bugs galore riddle this game, and there's no where to report problems to, no one to send screenshots and information about them back to.

The problem that's a glaring one though, and the one that will 100% kill this game, is the fact that on top of the pay walls, there's not enough players to even fill a group on mid-tier content in advanced access.  I don't think that full release is going to change that dramatically, so when high-tier raids and co-ops are being matched for they're going to be all NPCs, and the end result is going to be near-impossible to complete.  The NPC AI is dumber than starfall's NPC AI, and at least those were comical.  This just feels like the developers were given a directive and they completed it as fast as possible without trying.  It also feels that this was greenlit as another attempt by a C-suite to cashgrab as much as humanly possible on the IP before people give up on it, like companies are doing with just about every other major IP right now.  I'm disappointed, and the players deserve better.  

Shame on you bandai namco.

Longer review:

At best this is a 5/10 game and I'm being extremely generous. The content is dire and itemisation is WORSE than games from early 2000. Even a game like Everquest in 1999 had better itemisation... I'm not even sure how people can leave any positive feedback just because of that. Farming is only interesting if looting/builds/itemisation is interesting, that's not the case here.

Weapon / Equipment are tied to your player level. They drop at your player level (or the maximum level that the quest is allowing). So if your player level is 53, you do a quest with a 50 cap, you'll get Lv50 items. If you do a quest with a 60 cap, you'll get level 53 items.

Pretty much all the gear you get is obsolete as you level up your player rank, there's no point in using currency/material to enhance your gear as you constantly find someone better as you level up. Enhancing is stupid and barely gives any boost anyway, we're talking like +0.5% damage or something per enhance. The max I did is +7 so far, looks like it can go up to +10. Like wow a whole +5% damage, amazing!!

You can also extract specific stats from Epic/Legendary items (like ATK UP+5%) and meld it back on another item. That's the only "real" customisation available, but most bonuses are too specific to be useful. Like +6.5% damage on Frozen enemies, like over a 20 minutes mission you'll hit maybe frozen enemies for a grand total of 2 minutes (and i'm being nice), so that's +6.5% damage @ 10% uptime = +0.65% overall DPS, pointless bonus...

The Co-Op quests are just copy/pasted and follow the same routine. You and your 4-players party (likely full of bots because the game is already dead on arrival) will start in an area, you'll fight through it, then this area merges into a general areas where all 5 parties meet together (20 players), then you proceed to a final area and the boss.

Being 2nd or 20th DPS wise yield the same reward, absolutely 0 reason to put any effort unless you're MVP. And even MVP get only a very small increased reward, the incentive is poor.

The gameplay loop is really basic, you'll keep repeating the same co-op quest until your player rank is high enough to move up to the next tier. In between there are 3 boss co-op quests (which are just the same you fought in the story anyway). Entire game content consist in:

* 5 Story Chapters, a total of about 35~ Missions.  (The story is crap, I'm sorry if you find that good, maybe you should try opening a book, just about any average book released in the past year will have a more enticing story)
* 9 Co-op quests re-using the environment seen in the story, pretty much all tunnels/corridor, even the "forest" is just corridors out in the open...
* 3 Boss co-op (same boss seen in story mode, nothing challenging also, mechanics are garbage, just dodge the run stuff on the ground wow... impressive)
* Free Roam, which consist of couple very large and mostly empty maps where the 5-6 same type of monsters will spawn. The map is split across several region tied to a level range.
* An "infinity tower", where you fighting few waves of monsters and try to survive alone. You need to clear each floor 5 times which 5 different character to move up to the next floor. That mode is most brain dead ever, even less strategy than... Genshin  Impact Abyss.

And that's it. This game only has the above.

Do yourself a favour, buy GBF Relink instead. And if you want a good story (because ReLink story isn't that good either to be honest), buy a book alongside your game. But this SAO is worse that Fatal Bullet. My only positive are: no framerate issue, no crash, server was pretty stable for me (i.e. no disconnect during the game), loading times are acceptable, controller works straight out of the box (I use a Dual Sense).
20-30 minute queues for any multiplayer quest is ridiculous only a month into the games release, something has to change or its going to become impossible to play coop or raids

This is a massive downgrade from Alicization Lycoris. I own most of the SAO RPGs and while most of them are pretty similar, Alicization lycoris felt like they took a huge step forward. It's follow up game was more linear and felt like it went a bit backwards, but was still decent. Now we reach this Fractured Daydream and it's lost all the charms of previous games. 

You no longer feel like you are experiencing the SAO world like previous games. You drop in dungeons or raid bosses with other players which is unique to this game in the series. The only issue? It's insanely repetitive. Prior to Alicization Lycoris the maps were pretty small and linear but working through each one and its few side quests felt fulfilling. You advanced a silly side story that added silly new quirky side characters. It was fun! This game is not fun. It's boring, you spend hundreds of hours replaying the same 3 dungeon layouts and fight the same 3 raid bosses. 

Even worse they gate most of the raid bosses behind account level. You need like account level 80 to fight the last 2 unique raid bosses. This means you will be stuck farming the other two early raid bosses several dozens of times to level up your account. 

Progression is relatively weak too. You no longer play your own character and build it how you like, which has been a staple of the series. Now you need to level individual characters which are locked to a single weapon type. Each mission or boss is it's own encounter starting you at level 1. Meta progression in the form of weapon and accessory upgrades are very underwhelming. Besides main stat on gear they have additional bonuses except 95% of them are lack luster or useless and even the better ones barely add any noticeable bonus. 

Considering all these awful issues with the game the developers have the gall to release $20 character packages that add basically nothing to the game. It's a bloody joke. I hope this game did abysmal so they learn their lesson.

I'm going to go pretty in depth on this one. But the first thing I have to say is that the game, without bugs, would be a lot better

Consistent bugs - Game locks up at some point during multiplayer *after warning you that disconnecting can cause you to be punished* - I can very much imagine i'm going to suffer from that eventually, cause i have to keep restarting my game to have it move again.

- Game doesn't let me use abilities that are hold down abilities all of the time. It just skips the input. Doesn't do a normal attack, doesn't do anything, just doesn't work. Does this for both mouse one, mouse2, and on the gamepad. If i could change the inputs to a specific key, I suspect it'd work, because the trigger is likely being interrupted. One of the heavy downsides of unreal, and it's reactive system.

-Your idiotic teammates literally are slowed and do far less if you aren't watching them at all times. And I mean that literally. If they aren't on your screen, they literally move slower, and will not be able to keep up to you. If you want help, you have to keep them in view at all times.

The game itself is pretty solid, storyline wise. The play control (if working as intended) is pretty decent. It's short, as you can see with other reviews. Supposedly about 20 hours of play time. Not too bad, but might want to grab it on a sale for all of the other issues as well. The coop game play is limited to boss raids, free roam, and 'coop' which ends up being a boss rush. All of the players will sprint to the finish as quickly as possible, because that's pretty much how it's designed. It's not a great wife/husband game for this reason, really. If they'd made it coop through the story, it'd probably have worked better.

Tl;Dr - Could be a great game, has a lot of buggy issues. Coop could be better, for a game designed to be multiplayer and online only. If they ever shut down the services, this game is going to be pretty gutted. But you might still be able to play the story mode alone.
