A Horrible SAO Game—The Worst So Far, in My Opinion

This game is a disappointment. Although the story is quite interesting, that’s not why most of us bought it. It was marketed as a multiplayer experience, but it’s barely even a skeleton of a proper SAO game.

There’s no skill customization, and you end up grinding the same maps for hours on end. You keep playing, hoping it will improve, but it never does. If these were the only issues, it might still be bearable, but there are so many poor design choices that they completely ruin everyones experience.

There isn't much else to say, except that even if you're a die-hard SAO fan, you should skip this title—unless, of course, you're a fan of mindless grinding and don’t value your own time. In that case, you have my blessing.

Cheers

Personally I enjoy this game, but it’s held back by many issues that prevent it from being a worth buying for full price. If you can get it on sale I'd say in it's current state it's worth half of what it's asking for.

The core concept of the game is fun, and I do enjoy the world of SAO.
Some skins can be unlocked through the trial pass system, which is a positive step in the right direction. This is the best SAO game that's been released so far so for previous players of the series this is definitely a step up.

The long queue times, poor combat mechanics, overpriced DLC's/outfits in-store, and grindy progression system make it hard to recommend. If you’re a die-hard fan of the series, it might still be worth checking out on sale, but for most players, there are better, more polished games out there that offer a better experience for your money. If interested I will go more indepth into each of the issues below.

Long Queue Times, and Error Codes-
Queue times are absurd, primarily because there aren't enough players to fill the mid-level queues. As you level up, you'll unlock higher-level content, but good luck finding players for anything other than the lowest or highest-level queues. Even then, you’ll be waiting for a long time. It feels like matchmaking is broken, especially in mid-level content, where it’s near impossible to find a group. Imagine spending 10 minutes in que only to get an error code kicking you from the game after you do losing every drop you were picking up? Frustrating.

Pricing, and Value-
The game is overpriced for what it offers. The premium edition is $100 USD, and the base game is $60—both are too steep given the content and quality. On top of this, they’ve started releasing costume set DLCs that aren’t included in any of the editions. The deluxe edition includes the Season Pass Vol. 1 (Which if bought separately costs an additional $25), but it only includes 3 characters, which is a bit outrageous considering the cost. This also implies we'll see more Season Pass type DLC's which I assume will be the same price with the same amount of content in the future making an already expensive game even more expensive.

Grindy, and Short Trial Limits-
The trial time limits are too short for the grind that it requires unless you're willing to play hours daily. Weeklies unlock over time. If you put in the effort to clear them as they come out then you will most likely have to replay roles in the same missions in the following weeklies but if you wait for them to unlock then you now have a giant plateful to do all at once with only a few missions overlapping to be done at once. If you’re unlucky with matchmaking, you might end up spending hours just trying to complete a single mission for the Trial. Some missions are near impossible to finish like Syncro Counter's. For example in Boss Raid 1 triggering the Syncro Counter is nearly impossible if your teammates deal too much damage too quickly which is often the case since high level accounts will grind these out. If it does trigger you have a high chance of missing out still as some people might be camping it in order to get their missions done. Syncro as a Tank 5 times? Good luck getting there before everyone else.

In-game Store Issues, and Skin DLCs-
The highest-tier edition should offer access to every skin DLC or at least some in-game currency to buy ONE. Unfortunately, it doesn’t. Instead, you’ll have to buy “Medals” with more real money to purchase skins. While you can earn some skins via trial passes, the number of tickets awarded is small. One round of the trial pass so far has given you 1-2 tickets, and you need 3 tickets to unlock a decent skin set. I will commend them on not making the trial pass cost money so there's that.

Combat, and Controls-
Combat feels stiff, and the lack of control during attacks is frustrating. When you initiate an attack, it locks you into the animation for the full duration, and if there’s another enemy close by, you can’t immediately shift your focus to them even after finishing off an enemy with the first hit in the chain. You’re forced to finish the entire animation, even if you’re attacking air. The camera is a mess, especially when fighting flying enemies. The camera can spin uncontrollably during fights, making it hard to track your target. Additionally, One of the flying Boss enemy type's in free roam often will float out of reach becoming impossible to fight unless you’re a flying character or a gunner.

Free Roam, and Zone Issues-
The free-roam zones are poorly designed. There's a lot of empty space which means you'll be running around more than anything looking for enemies to fight which sometimes the red dot indicators for the boss enemies end up being wrong. Very rarely will you be put into an actual party with other players. Enemies from higher-level zones can follow another player into lower-level areas switching their target to you when that player get's out of their range. The fact that the Level 90 zone shares a line with the 1-18 section is a big issue involving this. When you die, you lose one of your acquired drops, which feels like an unnecessarily harsh penalty. Reviving other players is often not worth the risk when the enemies in the higher level zone can 1-2 hit you, especially when the revive button conflicts with attack presets on the controller, causing frustrating controls issues just to start the delay before the revive bar starts.

Co-op Play Problems-
The co-op play system is seriously flawed especially in Boss mode. In most cases, reviving a downed player doesn’t benefit you, especially since the game often rewards MVP teams based on damage output. If a player is down, it’s more beneficial to ignore them so their team loses damage so your team can get ahead. This leads to bad teamwork dynamics, where players abandon their teammates to get ahead for personal gain. The missions that pop up in Boss mode that give big chunks of score also are an issue. Highest combo mission for example. Players won't hit the Switch/Combo pop-up's when this mission is up because it will break their combo most of the time. No one going for the combo will stop to revive an ally either. There are also issues with treasure chests in co-op missions; since opening them doesn’t contribute to your score, most players just rush past them, ignoring the underwhelming loot that drops in co-op quests. This undermines the cooperative experience, and atmosphere the game should be promoting. My biggest issue with this system is players are starting to rush to the boss portal in co-op quests, and then waiting for everyone else to do the missions in the area so they can jump through the portal to start the boss before anyone else can get there so that they inflate their damage done.

Limited-Time Codes, and Outfits-
There are too many limited-time codes with a short duration, and they’re often poorly advertised. If you miss out on a code, you’ll never get that outfit/item again. The in-game outfits also don’t look very good, with some of the character models feeling a bit off—arm joints often look strangely pinched or awkward.

There's more issues especially involving Story Mode but for now I will end this review. I'll update it as the game continues to change.

A live service game that asks for full price at the door. 

The single player component is 10-15 hours of braindead-easy hack & slash with the typical simplistic writing you normally see in anime crossover games. The single player component alone might be justifiable at $5-10 if you're a big SAO fan.

Multiplayer is lacking in obvious QoL features and endgame content. The playerbase tanked by 90% after the first month and never recovered. Games need 5 players to even start and it's a fight to achieve that. The game's matchmaking was region locked for months and forced most players to figure out they had to switch to the JP server to even find games and then always suffered lag for their trouble. There is no competent way for games to be filled due to all players being skewed between account levels that only affect stat inflation when mechanics could have easily been designed differently to full everyone into a smaller number of queues. The game isn't designed to deal with AFK'ers running in circles at the start of a level to get mission rewards when the rest of the room finishes. Games in progress only have a tiny window to fill and then you're stuck with 15+ NPCs that can't pull their weight and if anyone drops it compounds the slog. Levels are randomly generated from a very small pool of possible rooms so they get stale fast. All gear drops are locked behind RNG and key components of your build may take hours before the game graces you. Most builds themselves lack depth and most equate to the same skill choices regardless of character with barely any unique options for individual characters. Half the cosmetics are locked behind a brutal season pass system grind or absurdly expensive microtransactions. Most cosmetics are colour swaps of existing costumes or ripped straight from previous games. DLC characters are way too expensive.

Multiplayer should have been free-to-play and even then this is far from acceptable as a live service.

But uh, Silica is playable and I can change her outfits, so 10/10.

If I reviewed this on launch my only issue would've been the asking price out the door, but that comes with the assumption that they'd spare no effort in giving you consistent, high-quality content every other week or so to dip your fingers into and work towards at no extra cost.

Well that was true up to the high-quality part, I'll just list what they did wrong since the game launched, what mistakes made it worse and what they honestly should have done.

First of all the cosmetics are, most of the time, recolours or reused from previous games of SAO. That's just really dumb, while free for the most part you can ignore that until the "free pass" gives literal recolours with minor modifications as the main reward with maybe an accessory. Note that these passes give two 'actual' cosmetics, I'm not counting profile elements here, over the span of a 4 week period. That's it.

Granted, they release these packages with cosmetics in them, often themed after characters or events and while some are also reused or simple- they're unique and cool and sometimes coming with an in-game effect changing their ultimate skill animation for example. Unfortunately not only do these take 3 months a piece to even come out, they're not a part of said "free" pass. You have to either earn ONE ticket per 4 WEEK season, or pay some extra to get what you want. Do remember this game was full price on entry, plus the DLC characters all costing a lot individually.

Props where they're due, there's a lot of cosmetics by now but they're still bland or just don't work in most cases since you can't change the colours at all, since the idea of making alternate colours a separate costume exists you likely have dozens of dead in the water options that exist just to make you look stupid.

Secondly, the gameplay is actually pretty strong at first, every character is unique in function, achieve different roles, better at different things. They made each option meaningful even when they're in the same class. The animations are also some of the best we've seen in SAO's history taking their personalities and skill sets into account:

Kirito maintains his position with large sweeping movements that flow into each other, he maintains a torrent of hits naturally and it feels really nice to chain attack after attack. Leafa's kendo is shown through strong singular strikes, with robust form and deliberate strikes and gains speed/strength while airborne which is a nice metaphor to her character. Strea, one of the DLC cast- who has basically zero references outside her original game which more or less used general animations all the time, has incredible weight to her attacks, letting her sword guide her along for the ride- with nods to her in-lore abilities as an MHCP in Aincrad that sells her as a powerhouse.

That's all well n' good, all that effort is well placed and it shows genuine care but unfortunately the same 4 skills get old, and the only thing allowing them to change is barely unlockable and with the rate of updates it basically NEVER means your favourite character is getting any new variations or content towards their kit.

Speaking of, Equipment. It's the main means of farming in the game. Your player rank controls what equips are dropped, higher it is, higher the level you do, the higher the equip rank. They come in multiple rarities and you can dismantle them to upgrade equipment up to +10: which is the short version. Legendary equipment however gives bonus abilities tailored to the character's weapon which is cool, it don't change much but is definitely the most exciting part. This sucked originally but they actually added a means to inherit abilities into new equipment so honestly fair to them. Sadly however until you reach max rank all of that is dead in the water so you're saving all of what you get until it's worthwhile to upgrade them and dismantle your old stuff. It's pretty inoffensive, but a lot more can be done, such as weapon accessories, or even effects you can earn for "prestige", they haven't though.

Thirdly and probably the worst part if you read anything about the game is the player count. Now believe me when I say this game had 15,000 players PLUS going by PC numbers alone from its launch and beta test, that's cool- just hop in, find 19 other guys and let the good times roll. Unfortunately, remember I mentioned player rank? Yeah so that dictates what level of content you can do and forgive me not checking this but there's like 20 or so different individual levels, from rank 1 to 150. All of which have separate queues. This included with the boss raid modes which also have like 5 to pick from for different queues.
Not enough? Well, region is a thing too. On EU? good luck. Switch to Asia and worsen your connection significantly for a room 'cause at this current time, playing at any other hour that isn't peak for Asian players is a certified infinite 1/20 players found.
Credit again, the netcode is actually really solid in your own region, surprisingly so. Unfortunately it took like 2 months before I had to switch indefinitely to even get games at my rank.

That raises another issue by the way, newer players will never find games due to the abhorrent splits to the point that the day 1 crossplay means nothing. They can't rank up and do the missions where players are since there's no one to reach the minimum necessary. Higher rank players can answer SOS requests to join in which is nice but it's just a bandaid on a much larger issue.

So you might ask, where did all the players go?

Well aside the combination of reasons I just mentioned, it's because that while the content for cosmetics and your literal REASON TO COME BACK didn't exist, they add like no new stages or bosses at all. Since launch we've had 2 bosses that are actually new. The others were just existing models repurposed, and the other "new" one was a tutorial enemy that wasn't already a boss because I kid you not it had two moves for the sake of the tutorial but nothing else so it wouldn't function otherwise.

Story mode is okay, as in the story, the gameplay is horrendous it's just walking around doing single player stuff in a co-op experience- I liked the new characters and setting and it's really cool to see everyone interact who normally wouldn't. Naturally that was the main draw for me since I love this series a lot.

Solutions:

But yeah to fix the game it's actually pretty easy, first of all they make it free cause the player base is cooked, second they add 4 cosmetics to the pass where 1 is a recolour or whatever the hell they want and 3 of them are actually given time and care, also two tickets per season not one. Third is they unify the queues entirely, it's not that simple but there should be no more than three, split it three ways, and let the players who queued up VOTE ON A MAP RATHER THAN LISTING ALL OF THEM AT ONCE. Hell, make it two a day and cycle, anything to make it more streamlined. Same for bosses, three ways, cycle them as they already do. Fourth, every MONTH at minimum just add either a new boss or map to select from, ideally both- then remove one from rotation until the next season, that way you don't miss out on the cosmetics they drop.

And lastly, every month, as a last bonus, choose at least two characters who gets a different preset of skills. Make ONE skill different entirely that you can swap out, and all three originals (minus the ultimate since those are changed with costumes) can be given different secondary effects that you earn with rank like how legendary equipment effects already work. This would spice up people's mains a lot and keep it fresh.

Sorry for the essay but I can't recommend the game in this state, it has genuinely great aspects and potential with an awful live-service support system, every PR post is just a "fight this boss but purple for an ugly hat" and it's sad. I love SAO and fans will love the character presentation, but this game isn't worth it.

bought the game hoping for decent action game, didn't get that.

stayed for 300hrs to figure out whats good, what works, how it works etc.

in the end, the experience is layer 1 shallow, there is virtually no skill expression, and the gearing/content loop is absurd, although they're *attempting* to address some of it in *season 2* they are still not fixing the fundamental errors that make this game absurdly unfun.

>progression is complete dogshit

you will spend the first 70-80hrs of your game experience just trying to reach rank 100, post season 2, the grind to 50 will be reduced, but the worst part of it (85-100) will be untouched. there is also no-one playing the content of the lower ranks/world-tiers. CPU/bot lobbies are dreadfully slow and teach you nothing of the game, even worse, is that the content you're doing is Co-Op quests, which by r100 you will find out all the knowledge you have accrued is absolutely worthless as r100+ content is exclusively boss raids

>the enemies don't fight you

you either roll the enemies to death in half a second, or you find arbitrary ways to avoid or mitigate them entirely. this includes bosses, but with how bad the ping is, you essentially just smack a big wall until it kills you (you're only dying in EX) for an action game with perfect guards/dodges, you almost never use them (also a DPS loss.)

>the gearing is abysmal

in endgame, you will need to setup your build with a specific set of equipment with desirable traits. getting a legendary item, is pretty fucking rare (1 in 10 on average iirc) then getting the item for your class-type (1 in 6) AND then getting the correct legendary trait (1 in about 5 or so depending on the item) AND then you need to farm several legendary and epic items to take stat lines for to create a desirable item. for every character. for every build.

weapons are almost entirely worse as for most characters, 75% of legendary effect options are ass, and one is locked to a specific element. even then, you require a weapon of every element that character has access to, with desirable traits, desirable legendary effect, then its RNG whether or not its EX (objective 10% dps increase) and if its lv.98-100 (average loss of 1.2% per level iirc)

in my 300hrs, with what i consider to be extremely lucky (and i was always 4-stacking in one of, if not, THE fastest party on the entire game) i was only able to fully gear up 2 characters. (silica/eiji) most players will never get fully optimised gear unless they're 500hrs deep.

i won't even go into how some of the BiS traits like crit have like a sub 2% chance of even appearing on gear, or the fact blue rarity and below cannot be used to take traits from, as i'd be writing a 50k word international crisis report.

>combat is very bland and expressionless

all characters share the same attack sequence profile, there are no jumpcancels to take advantage of, guard/dodge cancels are often suboptimal and have an arbitrary cooldown between uses and are very clunky. every character essentially boils down to "find optimal normal attack chain, find optimal skill, use off cooldown and repeat" with absolutely no exceptions. a lot of the top-tier characters have basic skills that can be indefinitely looped for easy, free damage.

as expected, there are no hard execution characters, one resource heavy character who is bugged as fuck, a couple of gimmicks that are mostly shared amongst several cast members at the same time etc. combined with a lack of response from the enemies, there is just nothing satisfying or fun. again, basic overview, but i only really have negative things to add.

>balancing (not just character balancing)

the roster is horrendously balanced, from characters having easy damage that infinitely tracks and has no weaknesses to characters who carry every utility, to characters who literally do the exact same thing BETTER than another character because "lol", and some characters who are incapable of doing virtually anything. the balancing is an absolute mess.

element damage fundamentally in my opinion upsets the game balance entirely, and makes balancing the game impossible from a developer standpoint. element adds a flat 20% additional damage boost to any damage done on an enemy, provided you hit them with the element they are weak to. (relink anyone?)

where the issues comes in, is that all (besides 3) characters are missing at least one element from their weapon roster. and mobs, where present in boss raids, might have a different elemental weakness than the boss, and finally, the BIGGEST problem, is that all characters have at least one elementally-locked skill.

the issue here, is that certain characters now have certain parts of their moveset completely made redundant or useful based on ONE select piece of content. sometimes an ENITRE CHARACTER becomes completely unplayable if their missing element is the weakness of the boss in current rotation. even worse yet, characters can have legendary effects on their weapons to change their elementally locked skill into a new element, which is also fixed to one type only, and grants a FURTHER 20% damage boost vs. that element. making gearing and character power even more matchup dependant.

as explained earlier, its also completely unviable to use multiple characters for specific bosses/quests, as you would quite simply never gear them in time.

element simply makes or breaks your damage performance, especially considering elemental damage stat lines are commonly one of the best overall damage increasing options, alongside the elemental damage boost mod that can drop in missions. (elemental damage is also capped out to 100%... because fuck you in even more hyper-specific scenarios)

there's also stuff like skill cooldown on crit that breaks the game, but it is what it is.

so in the end, you will be playing a game that requires 70-80hrs before you can even properly start playing it, with extremely shallow combat, no progression, an endless grind that you cannot win, with poorly balanced characters and mechanics, whilst having a concurrent playerbase of under 300 people. yeah i'd probably buy it in a sale for a laugh in 5 years time.

[h1]Short summary[/h1]
[list]
[*] 60-100$ game with cash shop (always-online, predatory pricing, pay for advantage).
[*] Combat ranges between mediocre and fine (more on that below).
[*] Lazy RPG mechanics. Numbers bloat, you kill at the same speed.
[*] PC port is lazy. 
   [list] 
     [*]Keyboard+Mouse controls are atrocious (not just key mappings).
     [*]Default mouse sensitivity is far too low and sometimes the game ignores the setting I maxed out.
     [*]No ultrawide, or any features that benefit more powerful PCs
   [/list]
[*] Story has "exploration", but crazy amount of invisible walls makes it infuriating.
[*] Artificially grindy. Low drop rates, bloated item/stat pools, timegated battlepass that only progresses from daily/weekly missions. Some of them are really sit in lobby until somebody requests aid (not a common thing to happen right now). Most weeklies are ~15 runs each with specific class (a full set took me ~20 hours).
[*] No chat.
[/list]

[h1]Combat(5/10)[/h1]
Button masher with sub-par responsiveness.
[list]
[*]Clunky controls (just some of the issues, there's a lot more):
   [list] 
      [*] [b]Some inputs don't trigger on first press[/b] (e.g. reviving often takes 3 attempts, chained skills sometimes trigger immediatelly other times not). 
      [*] [b]Animations lock you in place.[/b] Some of them are long. You cannot steer them if enemy moves out (happens a lot, because most enemies move freely). You can only cancel basic 
attacks once every 10 seconds. 
      [*] [b]Enemies (and bosses) casually move out of your combos.[/b] Some enemies (not all) consistently just walk out of them, forcing you to chase with really clunky combos. Flying enemies are the cherry on top, because they both run do that and sometimes ascend making them impossible to reach with melee.
      [*] [b]Most attacks aren't designed to be avoided in real gameplay.[/b] There are usually multiple damage sources with no real rhythm to them. Inability cancel animations realiably (and having to use cancels to reach enemies that walk away) means you take damage you can see coming, but can't avoid.
      [*] [b]You can get stuck in enemy hitbox[/b] preventing you from moving in any direction.
      [*] [b]Combat movement and directional skills don't always follow camera[/b]. This is especially bad when enemies walk out of range, because your dash to close the gap can go in a random direction.
      [*] [b]Lock-on is garbage[/b]. It doesn't rotate camera to face nearby, it doesn't reliably have your character face the enemy, and prevents you from rotating camera.
[/list]
[*] Multiplayer combat severely reduces visibility.
[*] Telegraphs in few places they exist aren't accurate (you get hit outside of them) and several of Trommel (mecha boss) attack telegraphs aren't even close to where the boss hits.
[/list]

With all of the issues above melee feels like 2000s 3D platformer where combat was not the main point. Tanks, support, mages and such are just a name. EVERYONE is who is not a ranger is a melee.

Ranged combat feels much better because it's not reliant on character animations, BUT enemy animations are twitchy, so hitting weak-spots (the only way ranged character compete) is difficult. Lack of proper sound design makes guns feel like air-soft guns.



One thing I do want to praise them for is character skills and special action. I won't sugarcoat it, there are too many characters for all of them to have meaningfully unique skills, but a fair amount of them aren't JUST larger/stronger attack. There is some creativity in skill design.


[h1]Multiplayer (4/10)[/h1]
Multiplayer has several modes and experience is slightly different in each one, however the core is roughly the same everywhere. You compete with everyone (including your own team) for damage. 

There's no reason to engage in anything besides primary objectives, and even primary objectives that aren't related to doing damage don't increase your score (they give the score to all teams who participated, so it's 0 advantage). With no rewards for side content it should be no surprise everyone rushed to the boss and skips objectives like console activation. There are also optional objectives that boost score and they are also mostly about damage (like achieving highest combo or landing highest hit).

In theme of competition, "kills" for various objectives only count for person dealing the last blow. In free roam (the only mode where grouping up could make sense) you are punished for grouping up, as it results in significantly longer completion times.


[h1]Itemization/crafting(5/10)[/h1]
It lacks any real impact on gameplay, and the item/stat pool is very bloated with unnecessary duplicate items (2 item types for different classes having 95% identical stats pools) and unusable stats. Drop rates for highest tier of items and cosmetics is abysmal. Based on my runs/rewards so far weapon skins (basic recolors) drop at ~5% rate and clothing items at <0.4%.

It feels like everything RPG related was implemented as an afterthought to keep people in game longer. Other systems following similar redundant time waste support that theory. For example: it takes upwards of 16 hours (optimistic estimate) to max level on 1 character and you cannot really focus on 1.

Crafting makes another fine example, as you can level things up and extract/inject effects. 
Sounds good? Here's how it works:
[list]
[*] Effects can be extracted from Epic and Legendary items
[*] Adding effects to an item cost common currency
[*] Replacing an effect costs a currency I've only seen in Battlepass(not even enough to make 1 "perfect" item).
[*] Effects can only be added to items of same type (despite different items sharing identical effects).
[/list]

Due to the bloat, the odds of you good effects on Epic/Legendary are very low. By the time you reach level 100 (when crafting is no longer a massive waste of time), you might have enough to equip 1 or 2 characters. The money cost of upgrading items is roughly 30 runs worth and if you're upgrading a legendary, it's hundreds of runs.

[h1]Story Mode(4/10)[/h1]
I did not like the fact it is long (for how repetitive it is), and is required to unlock all characters. I couldn't skip it if I want to try every character.

The mode itself is similar to multiplayer, except you can switch between characters and there's "exploration" in from of random hidden glowy things that don't give you anything worthwhile apart being required for "S" rank. The one thing about the story I thought was cool is the explorable areas had a sort of secondary boss monster that drops cosmetics.

[h1]Always online and monetization[/h1]
Presence of cheaters indicates 2 things: this is not a server based game and it doesn't have to be always online (because it's not server based). Always online is only there to "protect" premium currency against cheats.



As mentioned in itemization section, you require an item only available through battlepass to replace items effects. If I was a betting man, I'd bet on this item appearing in cash shop a bit later.

This game has consumable "Lucky charms" that add extra drops. There are 3 in battle pass and you can buy more for 1$ a piece (6 packs) I'm getting Diablo Immortal vibes.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
If you can enjoy a fantasy of playign SAO with the level of game design of 20$ game, go for it.
If not, this is a straight ripoff. This game doesn't do anything better than competitors don't already do MUCH better. Some games manage

Which brings me to my second issue: the content is repetitive.
After finishing the main story (which is alright. Nothing too great, but good nonetheless), players can pick between three activities: 
1. Boss Raids (3 different bosses to pick from, take about 5 minutes to complete)
2. Co-Op Quests (a large amount of different maps to pick from, includes a boss at the end, take about 30 minutes to complete)
3. Free Roam (players get to roam freely across a randomly chosen map to collect treasure and fight generic enemies, 1 hour time limit but can be finished any time)

At first, these are pretty fun. The problem is, they all play the exact same in the end.
It gets repetitive real fast, and the only way to remedy this would be new content.
And the last time new content was released as of writing this review was two months ago with a new playable character.
Further DLC has been announced, but not even a release date is known so far.
And the problem with the new content is the fact that it is behind a rather large paywall. So it's also clear that it won't be able to keep this game alive.
Another option to keep the players engaged would be the battle pass system. Unfortunately though, these battle passes almost never contain any items worth grinding for.

But as long as player numbers keep dwindling and wait times stay this long, the game is already dead after just 2 months.

Most people who pick this game up will want to play Multiplayer.
But here's the thing... You have to play the single player campaign to unlock characters.

So you spend so much time in single player running/dashing just to get to the next objectives.

But here's the next kicker!!!!

Those maps are arranged by Player Level. That means if you want to gain the most exp for your Account, you'll always want to do the latest mission. Once you reach "end game," they decided to pair up two missions together in a single queue. So if you select it, it's random which of the two maps you get.
At first you'd think that's good for variety, but this also means you have to stare at the loading screens to figure out which map you are playing on in order to select the right element weapon for that mission. Even worse, some characters don't have access to certain elements. Klein for example, doesn't have access to the Electric element, so if you pick him and the map switches to the forest, there's nothing you can do about it and you are forced to play that mission suboptimally. 

Not only that, but as you progress through the player ranks, it gets harder and harder to gain experience for your Account. Which means you end up running the same 2 quests or bosses (which there are currently only 3, maybe 4 because they switch out the last remaining boss from only a queue of 3 bosses). 

Which again, You need to be a very high player rank just to select the highest boss to fight.
Think about that. You are stuck farming the same boss over and over again. 

The game is also EXTREMELY grindy, which wouldn't be a problem if the game was fun.
But some characters are just broken. For example, with Asuna it's almost always best to just spam Triangle while held down. Some characters play best just spamming Square. Completely nullifying their entire kit.

This game just needs to be fleshed out with more content to be worth $60.

- Gameplay -
The game feels a bit clunky to play. Hitboxes seems wonky. There's a lot of times where something hits me when I think it wouldn't or that something doesn't hit me when I think it would. It feels like attacking normally feels better most of the time, as skills don't feel impactful enough to be used in a lot of scenarios. Flying monsters are kind of annoying, because you can't change direction while attacking midair, but also because some of them just keep running away from the player. The lock-on camera needs improvement. It doesn't always center the target, sometimes the target goes off screen. 


- Game Modes -
The story is whatever, but I did enjoyed one specific part. Story stages are based on Coop Battle stages for the most part. The problem is that there is no indication of where the map ends in a story stage, so you end up wasting a lot of time walking around while trying to collect everything, although you can probably just find a guide for collectables now that the game has been out of a while.

Coop Battle is one of the main modes. Honestly kind of disappointed about this one. I kind of expected a pseudo raid like experience, but there's no mechanics at all. You just go from objectives to objective, meeting up with other parties twice, before fighting a boss. As of right now, you cannot get max level gear from this mode. Tier 1 and 2 serves are map introduction. Once you reach Tier 3, you get 2 maps paired per level range. This makes for a very repetitive experience, as nothing changes for over a dozen of Player Ranks until you can start doing the next level range. When you outlevel the last level range, there's no point going back outside of doing battlepass quests and farming cosmetics you may be missing.

Boss Raid is the other main mode. This seems to be the proper end game, although I feel like the clunkiness of the game brings down its potential. It also feels annoying to fight certain bosses as a melee character. Tier 3 Boss Raid drops the highest level gear in the game and also rotates on a daily basis. 

Extreme Boss Raid: I don't know. You need to be 90 to participate. After 80 hours, I just reached 70 and I'm starting to feel the burnt out. They aren't even permanent either, seems to be a weekend type of thing during specific time frames.

Free Roam: The idea is technically nice, but it doesn't feel as good as it might sound. From my experience, the place feels empty and elites are too spread apart. If you want to kill a few minutes and don't know what else to do, and you really don't have anything else, then I guess it's something.

Tower of Determination: Your tower type of content, except you need to be able to beat a floor with 5 different characters to go to the next one. It mostly just gives you gold on initial clears.


- Multiplayer - 
The game already feels empty. It's been a bit over 2 weeks since the game has been released and my rooms are usually around 5 to 7 players out 20, after a few minutes of waiting, even with cross-platform multiplayer. Unless you switch your matchmaking to Asia, then it fills up pretty fast, but I don't personally enjoy playing games with lag, especially when the game is clunky. You need 5 people minimum to start a run, as there is 5 parties, requiring 1 player per party.

There is an Aid feature that sometimes pops up, allowing you to join a match already in progress. This is a nice feature because it scales the rewards to your Player Rank and allow you to have a much needed change in scenery. The only thing that feels terrible here is when joining an in progress Boss Raid. Unless you happen to spawn in during a mob wave, you'll be severely under leveled until the next mob wave.


- Battlepass -
This feature is completely free. You can obtain 2 SAO Tickets per month, equivalent to 6$ USD each, and the cosmetics bundles are either 6/12/18$(1-3 tickets). The quests are fairly grindy, but at least you only have to get to 16 out of 28 levels for the tickets. 


- Settings - 
For some reason, the keybinds are not global. The keybinds are split into 3 types: normal, flying and shooting characters. When adjusting your keybinds, make sure to adjust them for all types. Also, the sensitivity seems to have some weird behaviors. It almost never feel like it should when you start a match, but generally seems to go back to normal after a few level ups..?


Overall, as someone that is tolerant and that doesn't mind grinding and repetitiveness too much, the game still feels kinda fun, but it comes at a high price, with a low NA playerbase, and it is feels very time consuming. That said, this is probably the closest thing we have gotten to a multiplayer SAO game, although I expect this to just end up being a skin platform.

TL;DR - I don't recommend this game at this price for the average gamer. For a big SAO fan, it does have it's merits - but at the end of the day it's [i]just[/i] a "good SAO game", but overall: it's a pretty mediocre game. At best it's realistically worth ~30 USD. Wait for a sale unless you're really into SAO imo.

Okay first off I need to rant about how dogshit the PC port to this game is, because the performance/gameplay issues are my biggest personal complaints. Here's some of the vErY FuN "features" you'll experience playing this game on PC / with Mouse and Keyboard:

[list]
    [*]Your mouse sensitivity will randomly decide whether it wants to actually use the settings you set or not. This makes playing gun characters incredibly inconsistent because your sensitivity will never feel the same between different maps / runs.
    [*]Your camera sensitivity will be tied to your FPS, so certain maps will fling your sensitivity to the moon when entering a new room unless you set your FPS to be locked at 60.
    [*]Skill direction will be decided on your character's position instead of your mouse/camera's direction. So if your character is facing to the left, and you try to aim your mouse forward to use a skill in that direction: the skill will just go to the left. You need to move in a direction before using 90% of skills. There are a handful of skills that can be aimed with the mouse, but if you're playing on mouse and keyboard it'd feel more natural for all skills to be aimed with the mouse.
    [*]Targeting is awful, and "aim assist" is actually just a janky aim debuff on mouse/keyboard. To consistently hit the things you actually want to hit, you need to turn off automatic targeting and constantly untarget/retarget mobs while ONCE AGAIN needing to "aim" your targets with character movement instead of mouse/camera direction.
    [*]Flying characters feel janky as hell due to the combo of bad targeting and in-air movement also feeling clunky. It's not very easy to move your character up/down in the ways that you want to try and target a weak spot on a boss, for instance.
[/list]

This might seem like a kinda nitpicky list of issues, but consider that these are all fundamental parts of combat. At the end of the day this is a grind game, so combat is going to be 90% of what you do. If that combat is janky and buggy as hell for people who feel more comfortable on mouse and keyboard, then obviously the relatively small issues are going to feel fucking horrible when you've been dealing with them for the 90-100 hours it takes to unlock the highest level of content. Which speaking of: the grind.

The grind in this game is kinda awful. Like I said, it takes roughly 90-100 hours of dedicated grind to get to level 90 (with a max of lvl 100, so add another ~10hrs), which is the required level for taking on EX Raids. These are limited timed raids that only last for a few days whenever the dev team decides to run them, and they're only live for 3 hour intervals every few hours. You can't respawn in these raids, and many mechanics one-shot you, so it's basically a challenge mode with the only reward being a random CHANCE at a recoloured cosmetic. It's kinda neat, kinda disappointing (slogan for the game).

So what do you do for those 90-100 hours of mindless grind? Well, for the first 85-90 hours you spam the same 1-2 highest level co-op quest maps you have access to (there's a total of 6 maps in the game, but only 1-2 are relevant for your leveling at any given moment) until you hit level 85. After that, you spam Tier 3 raid bosses which rotate between 5 different raid bosses daily. There's 2 other raids you have access to earlier in the game, but they're not very worth doing for pure leveling. The bosses range from pretty neat, to kinda eh. If you've played actual MMOs, they're all pretty simple tbh. 

At the start of the game, you have access to 21 different characters, and leveling characters to 30 will unlock their passive to be used for other characters (only 2 equipable on a chara at a time). This incentives you to play different characters while leveling to try and get good passive for your mains. And honestly, that's probably a good thing. The characters and their kits are probably the most fun part of this game. Most characters play very differently from each other, and many of them have very fluid kits (once you cope with the dogshit targeting and being forced to aim your skills with movement, of course). Honestly the only thing that helped me push to keep grinding this game which was how fun and different the characters can feel to play, and seeing the interactions between different heroes/villains from across the SAO series.

oh and the story is... fine? again, neat for SAO fans - nobody else will probably care. you have to play through like ~2-4 hours of it (while spamming) to unlock all the characters for multiplayer content. going back while not spamming/skipping cutscenes leads to much longer playtime ofc. not much to say on it, just kinda fine.

so.. yeah. secondary tl;dr - game is meh and grindy with a shallow pool of maps/bosses, characters are fairly diverse with some fun kits, lots of neat character interactions for SAO fans, there's a lot of AFKers and they're all cringe, Eiji / Yuuki / Heathcliff are the most fun characters, and there's plenty of better grind games to play tbh but this one is decent-ish and SAO themed :3 ok bye
